headline: A 2014 House resolution would have condemned how a committee chairman ran a March 2014 hearing, but the House voted to table it and it did not pass.
what_it_does: H.Res. 504 was a question of the privileges of the House, a type of resolution that can be raised on the floor. It would have condemned Chairman Darrell E. Issa for the way he conducted the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee hearing on March 5, 2014. The resolution describes him turning off the ranking member's microphone while she was speaking and ending the hearing without a vote or unanimous consent. Because the House voted to table it, the resolution did not move forward.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee
who_it_affects.how: The resolution would have formally criticized the committee chairman and the ranking member's treatment during the hearing.
The resolution would have put a formal House condemnation of his conduct at the March 5, 2014 hearing on the record.
